title: Quantifying uncertainty of tuberculosis drug susceptibility range from single-microplate test
author: Postnikov, Lavrova

steps.title: Create enhanced fluorescence ensemble
steps.instruction: For each drug concentration collect the eight well fluorescence readings Fij and the eight control readings Fi0 (no drug). Compute the relative fluorescence for every possible pair as fij = Fij / Fi0, yielding 64 independent values per concentration. This forms the enhanced statistical ensemble used instead of a single averaged point.

substeps.instruction: Identify the eight measurements {Fij} for the test wells (i = 1…8) and the eight control measurements {Fi0} from the untreated column.
Calculate fij = Fij ÷ Fi0 for each of the 8 × 8 = 64 combinations.
Record all fij values; they serve as the data set for subsequent analysis.

steps.title: Transform data to Fisher‑Pry scale
steps.instruction: Convert each relative fluorescence fij to the Fisher‑Pry variable FP9 and pair it with the natural logarithm of the drug concentration (ln x) for linear regression.

substeps.instruction: Use the definition f = fij (relative fluorescence). By construction fmin = 0 and fmax = 1.
Compute FP9 for each point using Eq. (4): FP9 ≡ ln(1 − f) / ln(9) − 1.
Calculate ln (x) where x is the nominal drug concentration of the well (log‑base e of the serial‑dilution concentration).
Exclude unreliable points: discard any observation with f ≥ 1 (i.e., f > 0.9) or f = 0, because they lie outside the recommended interval 0.1 ≤ f ≤ 0.9 for linear fitting.
For each concentration, determine the 0.05 and 0.95 quantiles of FP9. Keep concentrations that satisfy:
• maximal concentration: 0.95‑quantile < 0,
• minimal concentration: 0.05‑quantile > 0,
• and any concentration that contains points crossing FP9 = 0.
Proceed only if at least two concentrations meet these criteria.

steps.title: Robust linear regression (order 1)
steps.instruction: Fit a straight line to FP9 versus ln (x) using a robust bisquare‑weighted polynomial of order 1 and compute the prediction interval for the zero‑crossing point.

substeps.instruction: In MATLAB call the ‘fit’ function with model 'poly1' and options:
• Robust = 'Bisquare',
• RobustWeight = 'Bisquare',
• TuningConstant = 4.685,
• MaxIter = 400,
• MaxFunEvals = 600,
• TolX = 1e‑6,
• TolFun = 1e‑6.
The fit yields coefficients a (slope) and b (intercept) such that FP9 = a·ln (x) + b.
Verify that the algorithm converged (exit flag indicating success; typical iterations 6‑34, median 11).

steps.title: Determine MIC uncertainty from zero crossing
steps.instruction: Calculate the concentration where the fitted line crosses FP9 = 0 and obtain its 95 % prediction interval, which defines the MIC uncertainty range.

substeps.instruction: Solve a·ln (x0) + b = 0 → ln (x0) = –b / a → x0 = exp(–b / a).
Use MATLAB’s ‘predint’ function on the fitted model with the argument FP9 = 0 to obtain the lower and upper 95 % prediction bounds for ln (x).
Exponentiate the bounds to convert back to concentration units (µg ml⁻¹).
Report the interval [x_lower , x_upper] as the MIC uncertainty range for the plate.
